name: Crustdata MCP Server
description: Search, enrich and watch people and companies from a single conversation in Claude with Crustdata. Build TAM, prospect and candidate lists using 150+ search filters such as job title, industry, funding and more. You can also enrich people and company profiles with 350+  datapoints such as verified emails, full work experience, education, funding, headcount, web traffic, job postings and more.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Crustdata MCP Server — B2B company and people intelligence platform (800M+ profiles, 200M+ companies).

TOOL SELECTION (use this order of preference):
- Company lookup: crustdata_company_identify_v2 (FREE) → crustdata_company_enrich_v2
- People search: crustdata_people_search_db_v2 → ONLY fall back to crustdata_people_search_live_v2 if it returns 0 results
- Company search: crustdata_company_search_db_v2 → ONLY fall back to crustdata_company_search_v2 for live LinkedIn data
- Contact info (emails/phones): crustdata_people_contact_enrich — THE tool for contact data; sync, up to 100 LinkedIn URLs per call. Use crustdata_people_enrich_v2 only for full profile data (work history, education, skills)
- Social posts: crustdata_social_post_search (indexed post dataset — posts by author, keyword, or engagement, with reactors/comments on request) → crustdata_social_posts_v2 (live, by person OR company profile) or crustdata_social_posts_by_keyword_v2 (live, by keyword) when the freshest posts matter
- Job listings: crustdata_job_search (filters/sorts/aggregations) or crustdata_job_search_live (realtime LinkedIn scrape by company)
- Web: crustdata_web_search_v2 to find pages → crustdata_web_fetch_v2 to read them
- Credit costs: run crustdata_credit_costs for the per-tool rate card before estimating spend — tool descriptions do not carry prices
- Batch jobs: crustdata_batch_job_search (async, every listing for up to 10 companies — no limit) or crustdata_batch_job_search_live (async live scrape, up to 10 companies)
- Alerts/webhooks: crustdata_watch_create (DEFAULT — profile changes on known people/companies, or NEW people/companies matching a filter) → crustdata_watch_list. Use the legacy crustdata_watcher_create → crustdata_watcher_list ONLY for LinkedIn posts, job postings, or person press mentions
- Discover valid filter values: crustdata_autocomplete_company_v2, crustdata_autocomplete_person_v2, crustdata_autocomplete_job (dataset searches); crustdata_autocomplete_filter_v2

tool.name: crustdata_company_search_db_v2
tool.title: Search company database
tool.description: COMPANY SEARCH — DATASET (/company/search, API version 2025-11-01). It replaces the retired crustdata_company_search_db. The primary company search: filter the Crustdata company dataset by industry, location, headcount, funding, growth, and more. Filter leaves use {field, type, value} with nested field paths (basic_info.name, headcount.total, locations.country, …); branches use {op, conditions}. Pagination is cursor-based (pass back next_cursor). Returns a markdown table by default; format='json' returns the nested records (compacted to key fields unless compact=false). Also filters on technographics (technographics.technologies.name / .category / .total_technologies), though crustdata_company_search_by_technology is the purpose-built tool for that.

limit.description: Results per page (1-1000, default 25). Combine a big page with `fields` to keep the response manageable.

sorts.description: Optional sorts: [{field, order: 'asc'|'desc'}], e.g. field 'headcount.total'. NOTE: the key is 'order' (a 'direction' key is auto-renamed).

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page (v2 has no numeric offset).

fields.description: Limit response to specific field paths (e.g. ['basic_info.name', 'headcount.total']). Omit for the full nested payload. Implies compact=false output shaping is unnecessary — you already chose the fields.

format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default) or 'json'. Markdown returns the companies as a compact table plus the pagination footer — use json when you need structured data for programmatic follow-up (e.g. extracting crustdata_company_id values).

compact.description: format='json' only: return trimmed records with key fields. Set false for full nested data.

filters.description: Filter tree. Leaves: {field, type, value} (NOT 'column'); branches: {op: 'and'|'or'|'all_of', conditions: [...]}. tool.title: Semantic people search
tool.description: PEOPLE SEMANTIC SEARCH (beta) — natural-language people search on the /person/search dataset (v2025-11-01). crustdata_people_search_db_v2 covers ordinary filter-based people search. This tool is for requests that ask for semantic / natural-language search specifically — 'use semantic search', 'natural-language search', 'search by description', 'rank these by relevance', or a pasted job description with a request for similar people. WHAT IT DOES: ranks people by how well their whole profile (title, skills, company history, education, location, summary) matches `query`. KEY BEHAVIORS: (1) It always returns results — the per-profile `fit` tier (strong / possible / weak) is the quality signal; the result count is not. (2) `total_count` is the size of the ranked pool, not a count of good matches. (3) Results are already relevance-ordered — sorting is not available. PARAMS: `query` (required natural-language text); `search_mode` (hybrid/lexical/semantic); `recall_mode` (managed/exact — use 'exact' to enforce `filters` as hard constraints); `query_syntax='boolean'` reads `query` as a keyword expression (AND / | / + / - / "phrase" / prefix*; lexical + exact only); optional `filters` (same tree shape as crustdata_people_search_db_v2, leaves use 'field' not 'column'). RESPONSE: a markdown table by default (with a Fit column); format='json' returns the native nested v2 shape (basic_profile / contact / experience / education / social_handles / professional_network) plus a per-profile `fit` tier, with top-level total_count + total_count_relation (eq | gte).

tool.name: crustdata_get_batch
tool.title: Get batch job results
tool.description: RETRIEVE AN EXISTING ASYNC BATCH by its batch_id — status plus results. Use this whenever a batch tool returned a batch_id instead of results because the job was still running: contact enrich, profile enrich, company enrich, job search, and person identify all funnel through it. It polls the job and, once complete, returns the records. It does NOT submit a new job and NEVER bills again — so when a batch times out, call THIS with the same batch_id rather than re-running the submit tool, which would start a fresh billable batch. RESPONSE: the API's job status verbatim — {batch_id, status (pending / processing / completed / failed), entity, action, identifier_count, result_count, entities_requested, entities_fulfilled, created_at, completed_at, error_message (failed jobs), download_url + download_urls (completed jobs)} — plus `results`, the downloaded records, once a completed job has any. While the job is still running, just call again later. An unknown or expired id returns a clear error (result files are retrievable for ~5 days after completion).

tool.name: crustdata_social_post_search
tool.title: Search social posts
tool.description: SOCIAL POST SEARCH (/social_post/search, API version 2025-11-01). Searches the indexed LinkedIn post dataset — the tool for questions about posts: what a person or company posted, posts mentioning a keyword, company, or person, the most-engaged posts on a topic, and who reacted or commented. Each post carries its author (with Crustdata id, title, employer, location), engagement counts, and on request every reactor and commenter. COST: billed per post returned; limit=0 counts matches for free (run crustdata_credit_costs for rates). FRESHNESS: the index trails the live network by days to a couple of weeks; crustdata_social_posts_v2 (by author or post URL) and crustdata_social_posts_by_keyword_v2 (by keyword) fetch straight from the network when the latest posts matter. A company's posts take two calls: crustdata_company_identify_v2 (free) returns the company's crustdata_company_id — every candidate when a name is ambiguous, so the right company is picked before anything is searched — then filters actor.crustdata_entity_id = that id with actor.actor_type = 'company'. Filters use {field, type, value} leaves; a keyword is text with '[.]'. Pagination is cursor-based. RESPONSE: a markdown table by default (with total and next_cursor); format='json' returns {posts, next_cursor, total_count}.

limit.description: Posts per page (0-1000, default 20). limit=0 returns only total_count, free of charge.

sorts.description: Sorts: [{field, order: 'asc'|'desc'}]. Sortable: date_posted (the default, newest first), engagement.total_reactions, engagement.total_comments, engagement.num_shares, post_type, actor.actor_type, and a few more.

cursor.description: Opaque next_cursor from the previous page.

fields.description: Dot-paths to return per post (list or comma-separated). Omitted: every group except reactors and comments. Add 'reactors' / 'comments' to get who reacted and commented (returned in full, so ask for them only when needed).

format.description: Response format: 'markdown' (default) or 'json'. Markdown returns the posts as a compact table (author, text, date, engagement counts, URL) — use json when you need structured data for programmatic follow-up. Requests for reactors or comments always return json, since the per-post reactor/commenter lists do not fit a table.

filters.description: Filter tree. Leaves: {field, type, value}; groups: {op: 'and'|'or', conditions: [...]} (a bare list is an AND group). Author: actor.crustdata_entity_id (a company id from crustdata_company_identify_v2, a person id from crustdata_people_search_db_v2 / crustdata_people_enrich_v2) together with actor.actor_type = 'company' | 'person'; a person's profile URL also matches on actor.professional_network_url (company pages are stored with a /posts suffix, so match companies by id: crustdata_company_identify_v2 first). Text: text with '[.]' (exact phrase) or '(.)' (all words, typo-tolerant). Other fields: date_posted (ISO date, with '=>' / '=<'), post_type, hashtags, actor.name / title / company_name / industry / location.country, engagement.total_reactions / total_comments, reactors.name / title / company, comments.text, mentions.company_id / person_id, content_type ('document' | 'article' | 'poll'). Operators: =, !=, <, =<, >, =>, in, not_in, is_null, is_not_null, (.), [.], has_all, geo_distance / geo_exclude (actor.location only). Omit for all posts.

tool.name: crustdata_watcher_create
tool.title: Create an event watcher
tool.description: LEGACY event watcher (v1 /watcher/watches). Create a watch ONLY for the three subjects the v2 system has no dataset for: LinkedIn POSTS (by keyword, by person, or by company), INDIVIDUAL JOB POSTINGS matched on keyword/location, and PERSON PRESS MENTIONS. For anything else, including profile or attribute changes on known people/companies and discovery of new people/companies matching filters, use crustdata_watch_create instead. Note this tool fires at most once a DAY (frequency is in days); crustdata_watch_create goes hourly, so a need for fresher data is a reason to prefer it, not this. notification_endpoint is REQUIRED and must be an HTTPS URL the user controls. Ask for it rather than guessing, and never point a watch at a Crustdata-owned host. Delivered payloads are also readable in chat via crustdata_watcher_run_summary, so the user does not have to build anything against their endpoint to see results. Creating a watch is FREE; credits are only charged when the watch runs. Event types include 'job-posting-with-keyword-and-location' (new job postings), 'company-watch-linkedin-posts' (company LinkedIn activity), 'linkedin-person-post-updates' (person LinkedIn posts), 'person-discovery-via-filters' (people matching Sales Nav filters), and more. Use crustdata_watcher_simulate to dry-run first, crustdata_watcher_cancel to permanently stop a watch. The response includes an `api_request` field with the exact JSON body posted and a copy-pasteable curl; after creating, surface that curl to the user so they can reproduce or save it. SEE ALSO: crustdata_watch_create — the NEW v2 watch system (entity + discovery watchers on people/companies data) and the DEFAULT choice for creating a watch; this legacy tool is the fallback only for posts, individual job postings, and person press mentions.

event_filters.description:
Event-specific filters. Example: [{"filter_type": "REGION", "type": "in", "value": "San Francisco"}]. 

TITLE MATCHING GUIDANCE (person-discovery-via-filters):
Sales Nav has two title-matching mechanisms with different semantics — pick the right one:
- CURRENT_TITLE (default): tokenized substring match across the current_title   field. Good for generic titles where you want variants — e.g. "Director"   matches "Sr. Director", "Senior Director, Engineering", etc. Ignores   quote marks; cannot enforce literal phrase matching.
- KEYWORD: full-text search across title + headline + summary that DOES   respect quoted phrases. Only one KEYWORD value allowed per watcher —   combine multiple phrases with Sales Nav boolean OR, e.g.   `"AI Founder" OR "Founder AI" OR "AI CEO"`.

Use KEYWORD with quoted phrases (instead of CURRENT_TITLE) when ANY of:
- The title contains a short 2-3 letter acronym (AI, ML, BI, HR, IT, RH, AD,   etc.). Without quotes Sales Nav strips dots and collides with abbreviations   like "a.i." (Dutch *ad interim*), "A.D." (German), etc.
- The user used quotes around the title, or said "exactly", "literally",   "the title is".
- The REGION is non-English (NL/DE/FR/IT/ES/PT/etc.) where abbreviated job   titles are common in business culture.

Note: KEYWORD doesn't count toward the 10k pre-flight cap, so a KEYWORD-narrowed search often needs SENIORITY_LEVEL + INDUSTRY + COMPANY_HEADCOUNT to bring the candidate pool under 10k before creation.

account_filters.description: Company filters. Filter types: INDUSTRY, COMPANY_HEADCOUNT, COMPANY_HQ_COUNTRY, LAST_FUNDING_ROUND_TYPE

event_type_slug.description:
Type of event to monitor. Pick the right family for the user's intent:

Person tracking (specific LinkedIn profiles — pass LINKEDIN_PROFILE_URL in event_filters):
  - 'linkedin-person-profile-updates' — profile/job/title/headline/location CHANGES
  - 'linkedin-person-post-updates' — new LinkedIn POSTS from that profile
  - 'linkedin-person-press-mentions' — press articles MENTIONING that person

Company tracking (specific LinkedIn companies — pass LINKEDIN_COMPANY_URL in event_filters):
  - 'company-watch-linkedin-posts' / 'company-watch-linkedin-job-postings' /
    'company-watch-funding-milestones' / 'company-watch-press-mentions' /
    'company-watch-headcount-growth'

Discovery — filter-based, find new matches over time. Each has specific filter requirements:
  - 'person-discovery-via-filters' — people matching Sales Nav filters; put filters in event_filters (KEYWORD, CURRENT_TITLE, REGION, SENIORITY_LEVEL, INDUSTRY, COMPANY_HEADCOUNT, RECENTLY_CHANGED_JOBS, etc.)
  - 'linkedin-post-with-keyword' — REQUIRES event_filters=[{filter_type:KEYWORD,...}] AND either account_filters or lead_filters (Sales Nav filters about author/company)
  - 'new-funding-announcements' — REQUIRES account_filters (INDUSTRY, COMPANY_HQ_COUNTRY, COMPANY_HEADCOUNT, LAST_FUNDING_ROUND_TYPE). event_filters can be empty or contain optional FUNDING_ROUND_TYPE. No need to identify specific companies first — just pass the firmographic account_filters.
  - 'job-posting-with-keyword-and-location' / 'job-posting-with-location' — REQUIRES event_filters with TITLE+REGION (or DESCRIPTION+REGION) and account_filters with COMPANY_HEADCOUNT / COMPANY_HQ_COUNTRY etc.
  - 'person-starting-new-position'
  - 'company-headcount-growth' / 'company-headcount-growth-over-baseline' /
    'company-department-headcount' / 'first-person-hired-in-company-department' /
    'first-person-hired-internationally' / 'company-employee-job-location-in-two-countries'

HEURISTICS:
- 'profile change' / 'job change' for a specific person URL →   'linkedin-person-profile-updates' (NOT post-updates).
- 'when companies in X raise funding' / 'funding alerts for industry Y' → go   straight to 'new-funding-announcements' with account_filters — resolving   specific companies first is unnecessary here.
- 'monitor company X's posts' → 'company-watch-linkedin-posts' with LINKEDIN_COMPANY_URL.
- 'people leaving company X' / 'who recently left X' →   'person-discovery-via-filters' with event_filters LAST_COMPANY (company   LinkedIn URL or domain, e.g. 'https://www.linkedin.com/company/openai/' or   'openai.com'; max 10 values) AND RECENTLY_CHANGED_JOBS. LAST_COMPANY is our   post-search filter that matches the person's MOST RECENTLY ENDED job — i.e.   the company they actually just left. PAST_COMPANY alone expresses a   different intent: it matches anyone who EVER worked there, including 10   years ago, so combined with RECENTLY_CHANGED_JOBS it returns people who   ever-touched-X-and-recently-left-anywhere. 'person-starting-new-position'   is also a different thing — it watches LinkedIn POSTS whose text says   'Starting a new position', not actual employer-change events.

tool.name: crustdata_watch_create
tool.title: Create a watch
tool.description: WATCH CREATE — NEW watcher system (v2025-11-01 API). Create an entity or discovery watch on people or companies. This is the DEFAULT tool for creating any watch: use it unless the subject is one v2 has no dataset for. The legacy crustdata_watcher_* tools cover exactly three such subjects: LinkedIn POSTS (by keyword, by person, or by company), INDIVIDUAL JOB POSTINGS matched on keyword/location (v2 carries only an aggregate hiring.open_jobs_timeseries count, not the postings), and PERSON PRESS MENTIONS (v2 has news on company only). Everything else belongs here: profile and attribute changes on known people or companies, and discovery of new people or companies matching filters. Cadence is not a reason to choose v1: v1 fires at most once a DAY, this tool fires as often as hourly. mode='entity' tracks known people/companies you list for profile changes; mode='discovery' alerts on NEW people/companies matching a saved filter. Entity mode: POST /watch/{entity_type} with entities + track (+ optional fields); billed per change notification (check crustdata_credit_costs) — person watches tier by config.refresh_frequency_days (fresher data costs more), first run is a free baseline and no-change runs are free. Discovery mode: POST /watch/{entity_type}/search with filters; billed per new match delivered, first run is a free baseline of up to 5 matches. Both modes need config.trigger ({type: 'interval', every_hours: N}) and at least one notifications channel. RESPONSE: {api_request, response} — api_request echoes the exact API call (with a copy-pasteable curl) and response is the created watch.

mode.description: 'entity' = watch a known list you supply (entities + track); 'discovery' = alert on NEW matches of a filter (filters).

track.description: Entity mode only. Condition tree for when to fire. Leaves: {field, type, value?} where type is 'changed' (scalar), 'added' (array), or a comparison '>', '<', '=', '!=', '=>' (>=), '=<' (<=) with value required; branches: {op: 'and'|'or', conditions: [...]}. Field paths match the v2 Enrich response, e.g. person basic_profile.current_title / experience.employment_details.current (added), company headcount.total (changed) / news (added). Fixed at create time.

config.description: Schedule + caps. 'trigger' is REQUIRED: {'type': 'interval', 'every_hours': N} (integer >= 1). Optional: 'max_results_per_run' (1-1000, default 25; discovery baseline is always capped at 5), 'preferred_hour' (0-23), 'expires_at' ('YYYY-MM-DD').

fields.description: Entity mode only. Field groups delivered in each notification's record (payload projection — does not affect when the watch fires or pricing). Defaults minimal: person basic_profile + social_handles, company basic_info. No wildcard; fixed at create time.

filters.description: Discovery mode only. Filter tree identical to the v2 person/company search: leaves {field, type, value}, branches {op: 'and'|'or', conditions: [...]}.

entities.description: Entity mode only. Map of identifier type -> list of values. person accepts only 'professional_network_profile_urls'; company accepts 'domains', 'names', 'professional_network_profile_urls', and 'crustdata_company_ids' (mixable). Up to 10,000 entities per watch.
